Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Jordan from Redwood Inference, AE on the account, joined by Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Marcus: Good, thanks. Marcus here. We wanted to run through our network constraints and see how Redwood would fit in our deployment model.
[00:14] Leah: Hi all. We mainly care about private connectivity, region residency, and the usual security checks.
[00:20] Priya: Awesome, thanks. Quick agenda — we'll ask about your current infra, expected traffic and latency SLOs, then go through connectivity options: VPC peering, PrivateLink/Private endpoints, and on-prem possibilities. Then we'll talk about encryption and KMS and close with next steps. Sound good?
[00:33] Samir: Yep, sounds good.

[01:10] Marcus: To give context — we run across multi-cloud, but primary is AWS (us-east-1 and eu-west-1). We have a bunch of microservices in private subnets, and want the inference calls to not traverse the public internet. We heard Redwood Private can do a VPC peering or use private endpoints?
[01:28] Jordan: Exactly. Redwood Private supports a few patterns: VPC peering (classic), AWS PrivateLink/Private Endpoints, or an egress-only NAT with a customer-managed VPN in constrained air-gapped scenarios. Peering is simplest but requires non-overlapping CIDRs; PrivateLink avoids route propagation issues but has per-endpoint costs and some regional constraints.
[01:50] Leah: For us CIDR overlap is a likely issue — our infra was carved years ago and a lot of nets are /16s. We don't want to renumber. Does Redwood support Transit Gateway peering?
[02:01] Priya: Yes, we often work with customers using TGW — Redwood can peer into a TGW, but it requires specific routing config and coordination with your network team. There is a doc we'll share that outlines required route tables, security-group rules, and AWS console steps.

[02:35] Samir: On the encryption side — all data at rest must be customer-managed keys and we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. How does Redwood handle KMS and audit logs in Private?
[02:45] Jordan: For Private we support customer KMS (bring-your-own-key) for model and data encryption at rest, and we expose audit logs. In hosted we have different levels, but Private gives you full control and log streaming options (S3, Kinesis, or pushing to your SIEM). We'll include the security whitepaper and integration notes in the follow-up.

[03:12] Marcus: Region question — we want inference to run in eu-west-1 for EU data residency. Do you have Private deployments there? Is there an extra setup time?
[03:22] Priya: We do. We support Private deployments across our supported regions, but there is provisioning lead time and sometimes hardware availability constraints depending on Dedicated capacity. Typical lead time is 2–4 weeks for a new private region deployment, shorter if you already have an account in that region. We'll check availability for eu-west-1 and confirm.

[03:54] Leah: Another question — latency. Our app needs <=120ms p95 for short generation calls (1–2k tokens), and we have some longer chat flows at ~4k tokens. How do we estimate expected latency with Dedicated nodes behind peering?
[04:06] Priya: Latency has multiple contributors: network hop between your VPC and the Redwood Private VPC, our model execution time on the selected GPU (and quantization/compilation), and token streaming. For p95 120ms on short requests it's achievable with a colocated region and dedicated capacity; for 4k token flows the absolute tail increases because of model compute — we usually recommend benchmarking with a sample workload. I'll run a sizing/latency estimate and share expected numbers for their model family assumption.

[05:00] Marcus: Good. Regarding auth — we use SAML SSO and corporate RBAC; how do you integrate with our identity?
[05:08] Jordan: For the control plane we support SAML/SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. For the Private control plane we can integrate with your IdP over the private connection, or use a federated auth proxy. We'll include our SSO integration docs.

[06:22] Samir: One more security nuance — we have an internal policy that prohibits peering with third-party VPCs unless there's a strict egress filter and flow logs enabled. Can Redwood support strict security groups/flow logs and we can push VPC flow logs into our logging account?
[06:38] Priya: Yes, customers often require tight egress rules. We can lock down endpoints to specific ports and CIDR blocks, and enable VPC Flow Logs on our side to be shared. We'll need to coordinate the IAM roles and log destination; again, doc in the follow-up.

[07:05] Marcus: Cost-wise, curious about the tradeoffs — Private + Dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted consumption. We expect sustained throughput but not huge spikes.
[07:15] Jordan: Dedicated reserved capacity gives stable unit economics and predictable latency, but it requires a commit. Hosted is easier to start but can get expensive at scale. For a pilot we often suggest a small Dedicated pilot or ephemeral Dedicated nodes to measure throughput; we can model costs once we know token volumes.

[08:00] Leah: Timeline and stakeholders — we're looking to start a pilot in November and go to production in Q1. Decision-makers are me + Marcus + Infra lead, and security sign-off by Samir. Budget approval process likely mid-November.
[08:15] Jordan: That's great, aligns well. We'll aim to provide the docs and pricing by Tuesday, and schedule the SE deep dive for next week.

[09:00] Priya: Quick technical clarifications — when you say private endpoints, you're referring to AWS PrivateLink vs our internal term private endpoint which sometimes maps to an ENI and private IP. For PrivateLink you need to create an interface endpoint in your VPC which connects to our NLB in the Redwood VPC. That has different routing and DNS implications than peering.
[09:25] Marcus: Yeah, we heard about PrivateLink costs per ENI and cross-AZ charges — that might be okay for certain services. If we use TGW, are there route table propagation caveats?
[09:36] Priya: TGW works, but you need to ensure route propagation doesn't unintentionally leak subnets. Also, TGW-based peering may require additional approvals inside your infra org. For CIDR overlap, PrivateLink is sometimes an easier lift since it's interface endpoints on your side with no global route table conflicts.

[10:05] Samir: Any support for on-prem or air-gapped? We have a small subset of workloads that can't leave the data center.
[10:12] Jordan: We offer an on-prem package for fully air-gapped environments — it's heavier lift and includes an operator bundle and managed lifecycle via your private control plane. That's typically an enterprise engagement. For the pilot, sounds like you'd prefer cloud Private deployment.

[11:00] Leah: Can we get an architecture diagram showing VPC peering and PrivateLink flows, plus example security group rules?
[11:08] Priya: Absolutely. We'll include diagrams and a checklist for network prerequisites.

[12:00] Marcus: For the pilot, the test data — we want to ensure no PHI leaves the EU. We'll scope a tokenized dataset and run evals. Is there a sandbox env we can use?
[12:12] Jordan: Yes, we'll provide a demo/private sandbox in eu-west-1 if available, or a hosted sandbox with a private endpoint to test. We'll confirm region availability.

[13:10] (discussion continues — clarifications around routing, DNS, split-horizon, and expected burst patterns)

[20:00] Priya: I'll outline steps we typically take: 1) Exchange CIDR ranges and accounts, 2) decide peering vs PrivateLink, 3) configure routes/security groups and a smoke test, 4) run benchmark with sample prompt set, 5) iterate on sizing.

[20:25] Marcus: That plan works. For credentials and audit, we need to know retention windows for logs — we have a 7-year retention policy for certain logs, is Redwood able to forward long-term logs?
[20:36] Jordan: Yes, logs can be forwarded to your S3 buckets or Kinesis and you can set lifecycle there. For audit records we can also forward syslogs to your SIEM; retention is controlled on your side.

[24:00] (there are a few instances of crosstalk, slight transcription errors — e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "KV case" at one point)

[28:00] Leah: Regarding entitlements and RBAC — can we map roles to our groups and limit who can deploy models?
[28:08] Priya: Yes, we have fine-grained RBAC and can integrate with SCIM for provisioning. We can also restrict model deployment to certain groups.

[33:12] Marcus: Any red flags we should consider around egress costs if we peer?
[33:20] Jordan: Egress is typically cheaper inside region peering but you may incur cross-AZ or inter-region transfer costs; PrivateLink has per-GB and per-ENI costs. We'll run a simple cost comparator given your expected volumes.

[36:00] Samir: Compliance check — do you have a SOC 2 Type II report and penetration test results we can hand to our compliance team?
[36:08] Jordan: Yes, SOC 2 Type II is available, plus a summary of recent pentest findings. We'll attach those documents.
